Study. Zhang J-R, Shen S-Y et al. “Augmented microglial endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondria contacts mediate depression-like behavior in mice induced by chronic social defeat stress.” Nature Communications 15, 5199 (2024). doi:10.1038/s41467-024-49597-z; full text. Original paper: CC BY 4.0.

Original figure. Published Figure 2 is directly embedded byte-for-byte. Panels 2a and 2c are displayed as crops; 2c microscopy and its chart are split and realigned, preserving the original group labels, data, axes and scale bars. Figure 2a and 2c are from cultured primary hippocampal microglia extracted from fetal mice and treated with ATP, not the adult CSDS mouse brain slices. The mouse and cell experiments are distinct models. Figure 2a: three mitochondria in three fields per condition; Figure 2c: n=4 per condition. TG, thapsigargin, is the positive control. Data are mean ± SEM. Figure 2a ATP vs control P = 0.0006; Figure 2c ATP vs control P = 0.0050. The figure and chart remain bitmap imagery, not individually editable data.

Mechanism and interpretation. The organelles, microglial cell and brain are conceptual artwork, not photomicrographs. The paper reports increased ER–mitochondria contacts and mitochondrial superoxide following eATP treatment. ER-to-mitochondria calcium transfer is a proposed mechanism supported by calcium measurements, not a directly measured flux in the displayed Figure 2a/2c. The mouse-behavior sentence summarizes separate in-vivo results (Figure 4); not all behavioral tests showed significant interactions. This is preclinical evidence, not a proven intervention for people.

Art sources. Mouse brain: NIAID BioArt, Ryan Kissinger, Mouse Brain, Public Domain; cropped in layout. Microglia: John Chilton, Microglia reactive, SciDraw, CC BY 4.0; scaled and combined with a magnification. Organelles: Servier Medical Art via Bioicons, ER and mitochondrion, CC BY 3.0; scaled and arranged. The source SVG cell illustration contains embedded texture bitmaps.
